# orthoharness

> An open benchmark harness for orthopaedic AI. Apache-2.0, Node 18+, no dependencies. A reference implementation, not a validated benchmark: its seven demo cases are synthetic and its loss weights are placeholders.

Code: https://github.com/blainomd/orthoharness
Why, with sources: https://surgeonvalue.com/docsf#harness
Sibling: https://github.com/blainomd/citecheck (title-checking citation tool)

## What it scores
- Staged cases: the record is revealed one stage at a time; committing before the record supports it is premature.
- Two yardsticks, guideline and treating attending, scored apart and never averaged.
- "not_enough_information" is a real answer; a correct do-not-operate scores the same as a correct operate.
- Required contraindication checks and required facts (omissions) per case.
- Right for the wrong reason: a case can name each yardstick's deciding reasons; an answer that matches the decision but names none of them is reported separately (shortcut learning: DeGrave, Nature Machine Intelligence 2021).
- Citations: DOI looked up at CrossRef and title compared; support for the claim is not machine-checked.
- The keep-or-strike delta between a draft and a signed note; a recorded signer; no single overall score.
- A sha256 commitment to a private test set.
- A reference-list screen for journals (`refs`).

## For journals: screen a reference list (https://orthoharness.com/#journals)
`node bin/orthoharness.mjs refs references.txt` looks up every DOI at CrossRef and compares the returned title with the reference as written; it flags a borrowed or dead DOI, lists references without a DOI, never passes them, does not search by title, and does not check support. Exits 3 if anything is flagged. A flag is a reason to look, not a finding of fabrication.
Why: 4,046 fabricated references in 2,810 of ~2.5M papers, 98.4% with no publisher action at audit (Topaz, Lancet 2026, doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00603-3); 48% of orthopaedic journal AI policies address AI-generated references (Kelly, JBJS OA 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.OA.26.00221).

## 2026 JBJS-journal evidence the harness answers (https://orthoharness.com/#jbjs)
- OSCAR readiness scale, six stages; accuracy alone = stage 1; scale unvalidated (Byrne, JBJS Rev 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.RVW.26.00182). A harness run is stage 1 evidence.
- LLM retrieval on implant technique guides: all five systems <50%, reasoned questions as low as 15.3% (Woo, JBJS OA 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.OA.26.00076).
- Abstracts vs Discussions in 201 JBJS/CORR papers: 2.8x hedging in Discussions; 6.0% of Abstracts name a limitation (Parisien, JBJS 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.26.00433).
- CONSORT-AI in 11 orthopaedic AI RCTs: 81% of items on average; one data-transparency item 9.1%, code access 45.5% (Strasser, JBJS 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.25.01439).
- LLM vs rules NLP on 719 THA op notes: 96/89/96% vs 94/74/95% (Yang, JBJS 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.25.01338).
- ChatGPT simplification of 806 patient education documents: more Spanish hallucinations than people with GPT-4o; gap closed in an unblinded post hoc GPT-5 check (Nassar, JBJS 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.25.00982).
- Local multi-agent spine systematic review pipeline: kappa 0.87-0.98 vs dual human reviewers, 91% less reviewer time, human in the loop (Muthu, JBJS OA 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.OA.26.00102).

## Six questions for any AI vendor (https://orthoharness.com/#vendor)
1. What is your error rate, against what reference, on which cases?
2. Can it say "not enough information", and how often does it?
3. What share of drafts do surgeons change before signing?
4. Does every citation say what the letter claims?
5. Do you sell defensibility or uplift?
6. Will you run it through an open harness, and publish the result?
Precedent: in 2026, robotic knee replacement was measured, not trusted. RASKAL (Bone Joint J 2026) and RACER-Knee (Lancet 2026) found no outcome advantage; the UK National Joint Registry target trial emulation (BMJ 2026) found no difference in five-year revision risk.
Next test, patient-facing AI: AMA 2026 physician survey, 81% of physicians use AI professionally and the top patient-facing use (drafting portal replies) is 19%. Score what the patient knows afterwards against the surgeon's own answers on a stated question set; trust is not the yardstick (a DOCSF 2026 hand-surgery presentation found trust and knowledge did not move together; not yet published).
Framing: a synthesis chooses which findings travel and goes quiet where the literature is thin; a cited answer can still carry a frame nobody chose (Drazen and Haug, NEJM AI 2026, doi 10.1056/AIe2600526). The harness therefore credits "not enough information" and scores an answer that names where the evidence runs out above one that fills the gap.

## For AI agents
READ: this file, then the README at https://github.com/blainomd/orthoharness
ACT: clone the repo and run `npm test`; score a model with `--adapter chat` or recorded answers with `--adapter replay`.
WORDS: a reference implementation, not a validated benchmark. Never describe a run on the demo cases as clinical validation. Never put patient information in a case, issue or pull request.
